ref.substituent_description: A 4-methyl-1,2,4-triazole (N-Me, three N atoms) is joined through its carbon next to the N-Me to C4 of a benzene ring; that benzene has OEt at C2 (ortho to the NH) and NH at C1 (para to the triazole). The NH is bonded to the ring N (N-N link) of a bicyclic 6-6 system that has a methyl (unlabelled line) on the pyridine-type ring and an azetidine N attached at the carbon next to the ring fusion; the azetidine has an unlabelled gem-dimethyl carbon next to N and a MeO-bearing carbon next to that.
ref.notes: Typeset structure. The bicycle has a pyridine-like ring (N=C, two C=C) fused to a ring containing a CH2, the NH-bearing N and one C=C. Double bonds: two in the triazole, three in the benzene, four in the bicycle.

wrong.substituent_description: A circled benzene has NH at C1, OCH2CH3 (O, CH2, CH3 written out) at C2 (ortho to the NH) and a 4-methyl-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl at C3 (the triazole ring has three N, an N-CH3, and two drawn double bonds). The NH is bonded to a ring N (N-N bond) of a bicyclic: a circled six-membered ring with one ring N is fused to a second six-membered ring (CH2, CH2, N, CH=C with one C=C drawn). On the circled ring, the carbon between the fusion carbon and the ring N carries a 2,2-dimethyl-3-methoxy azetidin-1-yl (N-azetidine, two CH3 on the carbon next to N, CH3O on the next carbon), and the carbon on the other side of the ring N carries CH3.
wrong.notes: Handwritten black ink on white paper. NH is written with H beneath N. Aromatic: circles in the benzene and in the six-membered ring with N; the triazole is drawn with alternating double bonds. Double bonds: two in the triazole, one in the fused second ring. The ring N of the bicyclic is directly bonded to the NH (N-N bond as drawn).

correct.substituent_description: A five-membered ring with two N (one carrying Me, two explicit C=C/C=N bonds) is bonded to a benzene ring (circle); going round the benzene from that carbon (position 1): NH at position 4 (para) and OEt at position 5 (ortho to NH, meta to the first substituent). The NH is bonded to a ring N of a fused bicyclic (two six-membered rings, ring N atoms in both) in which the other ring carries a methyl stub next to a ring N and, on the carbon on the other side of that ring N, a ring-N-bonded four-membered ring with MeO and two methyl stubs.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: two lines cross at the four-membered ring carbon next to N (horizontal line from the left methyl stub to N crossing the vertical bond), so it is unclear whether it is a quaternary carbon with two methyls or two crossing bonds
NH is joined to a ring N, giving an N-N bond as drawn
ring-atom vertices have small dots and the fused bicycle is freehand, so ring-N and double-bond positions are uncertain
correct.notes: Handwritten; crossing lines make the top four-membered ring hard to interpret. Double bonds: two in the five-membered ring, three in one six-ring of the fused bicycle, one in the other six-ring. Methyl groups are unlabeled line stubs (one on the bicycle, two on the four-membered ring).

ref.substituent_description: A central benzene ring carries, relative to the NH-bearing carbon (C1): the NH at C1, an OEt at C2 (ortho to the NH) and a 4-methyl-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl group at C4 (para to the NH). The NH is bonded to the ring N (the lower N) of a bicyclic 6-6 diaza-naphthalene-type system (one ring contains a CH2 next to that N); the upper ring of the bicycle has a ring N, a CH3 line (unlabelled) on the carbon next to it, and on the other side a 3-methoxy-2,2-dimethylazetidin-1-yl group (N-attached, CMe2 next to the N, CH(OMe) next to CMe2) attached to the carbon adjacent to the ring fusion.
ref.notes: Typeset drawing. Triazole: three N labels (two ring N plus the N bearing Me). Four unlabelled methyl line ends (two on azetidine C, one ring methyl on the bicycle, plus Me label on triazole N). Bicycle has four drawn double bonds (C=C, C=N, C=C, CH=CH); triazole two; benzene three.

wrong.substituent_description: The central benzene ring (drawn with a circle) is 1,2,3-trisubstituted: NH on the lower-right vertex (C1), an O-CH2-CH3 group on the bottom vertex (C2, ortho to the NH), and a 4-methyl triazole ring (5-membered ring containing three N, one of them bearing CH3) on the lower-left vertex (C3, ortho to the ethoxy and meta to the NH), joined through the triazole carbon that sits between the N-CH3 and a ring N. The NH is bonded directly to a ring N (N-N bond) in the left, partly saturated ring of a fused 6/6 bicycle; the right ring of the bicycle (circle) contains a second ring N, has CH3 on the carbon next to that N, and on the carbon on the other side of that N carries an N-linked 4-membered ring (azetidine N) bearing two CH3 on the carbon next to N and CH3O on the next carbon.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The left ring of the fused bicycle has one double bond drawn on the bond leading to a fusion carbon of the circled ring
NH is joined directly to a ring N (N-N link)
Triazole is drawn with Kekule double bonds while the benzene and the circled bicycle ring use circles
wrong.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white. Triazole has 2 double bonds, the left bicycle ring has 1; circles are not counted as double bonds. The ethoxy is drawn as O, CH2 (with a bond down) and CH3.

correct.substituent_description: A central benzene ring (drawn with an aromatic circle) carries, para to each other, a 5-membered two-nitrogen ring (attached through a ring carbon; its other ring N bears Me) and an N-H group; an OEt group sits on the ring carbon next to the NH-bearing carbon (meta to the five-membered ring). The NH is drawn bonded to an N atom of a fused bicyclic 6-6 system (one ring N at the fusion-adjacent corner, one ring with a C=N and a methyl line); that bicycle also bears, on the carbon next to its ring N, an N atom that is part of a 5-membered ring with an OMe on one ring carbon and unlabeled lines (methyls) on the adjacent carbon.

The bond between the NH and the bicyclic ring N reads as an N-N bond
Bicycle: double bonds drawn inconsistently (one ring has three inner lines, the other only one), short stub inside a ring
Unlabeled line ends (methyl groups) on bicycle and on the five-membered ring
correct.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white paper, very freehand. Double-bond count: 2 in the two-N five-membered ring, 3 in the upper bicycle ring (including a short vertical stub), 1 in the lower bicycle ring.
